questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I want to experience how it is to study abroad, how the school system is, get an experience for life, and try to live in another country.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Europe due to the fact that I could get Erasmus, it is close to home and easier process. And also the fact that I wanted to go with friends, and their first choice was Milan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, but some information was given after arrival. Which was a bit stressful at first hand. It is just important to remember that it will sort out and that other countries take things easier, but everything will work out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got regular emails on what to remember.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are many sites as for example Spotahome and Italianway which we used. It was quite easy, but it is good if you start searching as fast as possible to get the best deals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Milan I think it is the best option since I have heard bad reviews on living ON campus - i wouldn't do that. But it is important to be aware of scammers and use official sites.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got emails telling me what to do - it was quite easy, but still takes some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails to Massimo, who was very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to register for the classes. Although the website of the university can be a bit confusing. However, both the university and teachers were very helpful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax, everything will work out. You might need to change courses several times, but the teachers are very large.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was perfect.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit different, but that I also the fun part. From what I have heard, it is very different from course to course and faculty to faculty. Mostly oral exams or physical written exam. Also I experienced a lot more presentations, during the semester, than I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Digital Marketing and Innovation
Business History
Learning and Development
Governing the future: Goals and tools

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Business History: Great exam and also fun to learn about Italian business history. 
Digital Marketing and Innovation: interesting course bit many exams (3xwritten + 2xpresentation)

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't know. Didn't look into it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know. Some social activities. But because of the many Danes going on exchange in Milan, I didn't look into it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Dont know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take small trips to fx Bergamo, Lake Como or Parma. Also a weekend trip to Rome is highly recommended.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time to get used to the "chill" culture. But it is so nice, once you get used to slowing down, and think that everything will work out.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The chill culture and tempo.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is going to be the most amazing experience. Remember to enjoy every moment as much as you can.
Choose the courses based on what you find interesting. Also it is very different from course to course how much time and studying it requires from you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just living in another country and experiencing a different culture and different university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When it was coming to an end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I might have wished that I had taken the Italian lessons offered.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
